I told my dad I’d seen his Facebook message, but I actually muted him because he sends me chain posts all day. Now he’s asking why I never respond. Help me say it gently.

Our brokerage’s monthly report overstates the number of signed leases because I counted renewals twice. My manager says it’s not worth correcting since the difference is small. I’m uneasy about leaving it. What should I do?
My sister asked what I think of the logo she designed for her new bakery. It’s hard to read at small sizes, but she’s really proud of it. How can I bring that up without crushing her?
Our dog’s illness is terminal, and we may have to put her to sleep soon. My daughter is 5 and thinks the vet can fix anything. How should we talk to her about it?

We’re moving for my new job, and my daughter thinks we’re leaving because she had trouble making friends at her current school. How can I make clear this is an adult decision and not her fault?

I’d like a recommendation for a good hearing aid for my mom, ideally one that’s simple to maintain. She says her hearing is fine, but she often misunderstands the grandkids. Would you be candid with her about that, or ease into it?
I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder last year, and my teenager recently asked whether it runs in families. I want to be honest without making her worry that she'll develop it too. What could I say?
My neighbor brought flowers after my surgery, but they’re strongly scented and make me nauseated. Is there a polite way to ask her to take them home?
Do you think it’s fair to tell a client their campaign idea is unlikely to work, even if they’re excited about it and have already told their team it’s happening?
A friend tagged me in a post thanking everyone who came to their event. I left early because I wasn’t enjoying myself. Can you help me write a nice comment that doesn’t claim I had an amazing time?

A coworker asked if their demo went well. The app crashed twice, but they handled the questions confidently. How honest should I be in my feedback?
My aunt is excited about her new headshot for the county website. The lighting is unflattering, and she asked me to be honest. I don’t want to hurt her feelings—how could I phrase it?

My dad ordered a used car based on a seller’s description and hasn’t noticed a warning light. I think he should get it checked before paying the full amount, but he hates being second-guessed. How do I say it?
A friend asked me to help choose a profile photo, and she picked one where she looks tired and uncomfortable. Would it be unkind to say I think another picture shows her better?

I forgot to book interpreters for a listening session, and now several residents may not be able to participate. I’m tempted to say the vendor canceled. How should I tell my director what actually happened?

My friend is launching a clothing line with beautiful sketches but no clear plan for manufacturing costs. She asked if I believe in the idea. What do you think—should I be encouraging or spell out the risk?
Dad’s doctor told us his kidney disease is advanced, but Dad still believes a new diet will cure it. Our family is trying not to contradict him. How should I handle that conversation?

My advisor told me I probably won’t get into academia, and I’m still processing it. My parents keep telling my kids I’m going to be a professor. What can I say to the kids without either embarrassing my parents or pretending everything is settled?
We may have to put our elderly dog to sleep this weekend. Our 4-year-old keeps asking if the vet can make him better. Would you tell her plainly what might happen, or wait until we know for sure?
My brother is pitching a big family reunion trip that most of us can’t afford. He’s thrilled about organizing it. Should I tell him the plan probably won’t work, or wait and see what everyone says?
My dad submitted a letter to the editor and asked me to proofread it. It’s full of claims I know aren’t true. He takes criticism personally, so how can I approach it?
A friend’s graphic design portfolio has a few pieces that look very derivative. They asked whether they’re ready to apply for jobs. Do you think honesty is more helpful than reassurance here?

A resident complimented my work at a public counter and then asked me to “just make an exception” on their application. I want to respond warmly without giving the impression that the compliment will change the rules. What should I say?
Our elderly dog can’t go on the long family walks anymore, and my kids think he’s being lazy. The vet says he’s in pain. What should I tell them about his illness and why we’re changing our routine?
My father’s health has declined, and I need to ask my manager for a more flexible schedule. How much detail should I share about his condition in the email?

A former direct report asked me for a reference, and I know they’re currently dealing with anxiety. They also struggled to take feedback and needed frequent reminders. I don’t want to disclose anything private, but I don’t want to mislead the employer either.

Our community center rents rooms to local groups. A partner wants us to waive the fee because they’re also a nonprofit, but we rely on that income to cover utilities. Could you draft a warm but firm response?

Our club is planning a 24-hour charity gaming marathon, but the schedule has no real breaks for the people running it. I’m worried the organizers will burn out. What’s a constructive way to point that out?

My partner wants to build a tiny house and has sketched a plan that doesn’t seem practical for winter. They’re genuinely excited and have been feeling stuck for months. How do I discuss the problems without shutting down the idea?
I’m reviewing a classmate’s poster for the history fair. The colors look great, but the text is so small no one can read it. How do I bring that up tactfully?

I received a compliment from a caller who said I was “surprisingly articulate.” I can’t tell if it was meant kindly, and I don’t want to turn a routine support call into a confrontation. What’s a good response?
Someone at work asked if they look like they’ve gained weight. I don’t think commenting on their body is appropriate, but I also don’t want to seem evasive. How should I handle it?
Someone posted an unfair review that includes a false claim about our company. I want to correct the record without sounding defensive or revealing private customer details. Draft a response?

My employee has asked whether they’re on track for promotion. They’re valued, but they haven’t demonstrated the scope the role requires yet. Help me answer honestly and give them a concrete path forward.

A major donor asked whether our new food pantry location is definitely opening in September. We’re still waiting on permits, so it could be delayed. Can you help me answer without undermining confidence in the project?

Do you think it’s kinder to tell my friend that her online shop’s product photos look amateur, or to focus on the fact that she finally launched it? She asked for my honest opinion.

My friend has listed her home, and she keeps calling it “perfect” even though the photos show some obvious wear. She asked me to share the listing. What’s a supportive caption I can use without endorsing claims I don’t believe?
My team wants to buy a feedback handbook for new supervisors. Can you suggest a few qualities to look for in reviews so we don’t end up with a book that’s either harsh or all platitudes?
Is it kinder to tell a customer directly that their complaint is based on a misunderstanding, or to validate their frustration first even if that delays the correction?

We accidentally quoted a customer the wrong interest rate, and correcting it will cost them more each month. I have to call them today. Could you help me plan what to say?
Should I avoid mentioning a serious weakness in someone’s business plan if I know they’re already stressed and looking for encouragement?

Do you think it’s better to tell a child directly that a beloved pet is dying, or focus on the time the family still has together? My 6-year-old has started asking questions.
